## Learning objectives

- Enable managed identities and grant them roles
- Use `DefaultAzureCredential` and specific credentials
- Connect to Azure services without secrets

## Enabling a managed identity

```bash
az webapp identity assign --name app-shop-prod --resource-group rg-shop-prod
az role assignment create --assignee <principalId> \
  --role "Storage Blob Data Contributor" \
  --scope $(az storage account show -n stshopprod --query id -o tsv)
```

## Using it from .NET

```csharp
using Azure.Identity;
using Azure.Storage.Blobs;

TokenCredential credential = builder.Environment.IsDevelopment()
    ? new DefaultAzureCredential()
    : new ManagedIdentityCredential(ManagedIdentityId.SystemAssigned);

builder.Services.AddSingleton(new BlobServiceClient(new Uri("https://stshopprod.blob.core.windows.net"), credential));
```

```csharp
public sealed class InvoiceStore(BlobServiceClient blobs)
{
    public async Task UploadAsync(string name, Stream content, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var container = blobs.GetBlobContainerClient("invoices");
        await container.GetBlobClient(name).UploadAsync(content, overwrite: true, ct);
    }
}
```

Locally, `DefaultAzureCredential` picks up your `az login` or Visual Studio sign-in; in Azure, the
managed identity is used. No connection string with a key appears anywhere.

## The Microsoft.Extensions.Azure helpers

```csharp
builder.Services.AddAzureClients(clients =>
{
    clients.AddBlobServiceClient(new Uri("https://stshopprod.blob.core.windows.net"));
    clients.AddServiceBusClientWithNamespace("sb-shop-prod.servicebus.windows.net");
    clients.UseCredential(credential);
});
```

## Passwordless databases

```text
Server=tcp:sql-shop-prod.database.windows.net;Database=shop;Authentication=Active Directory Default;Encrypt=True
```

With `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`, `Authentication=Active Directory Default` (or `Active Directory
Managed Identity`) uses Entra tokens. Create a database user for the identity:

```sql
CREATE USER [app-shop-prod] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;
ALTER ROLE db_datareader ADD MEMBER [app-shop-prod];
ALTER ROLE db_datawriter ADD MEMBER [app-shop-prod];
```

## Workloads outside Azure

For GitHub Actions or Kubernetes, use **workload identity federation**: the external platform's
OIDC token is exchanged for an Entra token, again without storing secrets.

## Learning objectives

- Store and access secrets securely
- Load Key Vault secrets into .NET configuration
- Prefer identities over secrets where possible

## Creating a vault and granting access

```bash
az keyvault create -n kv-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --enable-rbac-authorization true
az role assignment create --assignee <app-principal-id> --role "Key Vault Secrets User" \
  --scope $(az keyvault show -n kv-shop-prod --query id -o tsv)
az keyvault secret set --vault-name kv-shop-prod --name "Payments--ApiKey" --value "<value>"
```

## Configuration provider

```csharp
builder.Configuration.AddAzureKeyVault(
    new Uri("https://kv-shop-prod.vault.azure.net/"),
    credential);

builder.Services.AddOptions<PaymentsOptions>().BindConfiguration("Payments").ValidateOnStart();
```

The `Azure.Extensions.AspNetCore.Configuration.Secrets` package loads secrets at startup (and can
reload them periodically). `Payments--ApiKey` becomes `Payments:ApiKey`.

## Direct access

```csharp
var client = new SecretClient(new Uri("https://kv-shop-prod.vault.azure.net/"), credential);
KeyVaultSecret secret = await client.GetSecretAsync("Payments--ApiKey", cancellationToken: ct);
```

## App Service and Functions references

App settings can reference secrets directly:

```text
@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://kv-shop-prod.vault.azure.net/secrets/Payments--ApiKey/)
```

The platform resolves the value using the app's managed identity, and your code just reads an
ordinary setting.

## Best practices

- Prefer managed identities to secrets; the best secret is the one you don't have
- One vault per application per environment limits blast radius
- Enable purge protection for production vaults
- Send diagnostic logs to Log Analytics and alert on unusual access
- Rotate secrets and use expiry dates; Event Grid can notify when secrets near expiry

## Learning objectives

- Host .NET web apps on App Service
- Use plans, slots and scaling
- Deploy safely with zero downtime

## Plans and apps

| Tier | Typical use |
|------|-------------|
| Free / Basic | Dev/test, no slots |
| Standard | Production basics: slots, autoscale |
| Premium v3/v4 | Higher performance, more slots, zone redundancy |
| Isolated v2 | Dedicated environment (App Service Environment) for network isolation |

```bash
az appservice plan create -n asp-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --sku P1V3 --is-linux
az webapp create -n app-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --plan asp-shop-prod --runtime "DOTNETCORE:10.0"
```

## Deploying

```bash
dotnet publish -c Release -o publish
cd publish && zip -r ../app.zip . && cd ..
az webapp deploy -n app-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --src-path app.zip --slot staging
az webapp deployment slot swap -n app-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --slot staging --target-slot production
```

In practice, use GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines with OIDC (workload identity federation) to deploy.

## Configuration

App settings appear to .NET as environment variables, overriding `appsettings.json`:

```bash
az webapp config appsettings set -n app-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod \
  --settings ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production Smtp__Host=smtp.example.com
```

## Health and scaling

- Configure a **health check path** (for example `/healthz`) so unhealthy instances are replaced
- Use **autoscale** on CPU, memory or queue length; set sensible minimum instances (two or more for
  production, ideally zone-redundant)
- Enable **Always On** to avoid idle unloading on dedicated tiers

## When not to use App Service

Very spiky or event-driven workloads may suit Functions; microservices needing sidecars,
scale-to-zero or Dapr may suit Container Apps; full Kubernetes control means AKS.

## A function app

```csharp
// Program.cs
var builder = FunctionsApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.ConfigureFunctionsWebApplication();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IInvoiceRenderer, PdfInvoiceRenderer>();
builder.Build().Run();
```

```csharp
public sealed class InvoiceFunctions(IInvoiceRenderer renderer, ILogger<InvoiceFunctions> logger)
{
    [Function("RenderInvoice")]
    [BlobOutput("invoices/{OrderId}.pdf", Connection = "Storage")]
    public async Task<byte[]> Run(
        [ServiceBusTrigger("orders-paid", Connection = "ServiceBus")] OrderPaid message)
    {
        logger.LogInformation("Rendering invoice for {OrderId}", message.OrderId);
        return await renderer.RenderAsync(message);
    }

    [Function("Health")]
    public IActionResult Health([HttpTrigger(AuthorizationLevel.Anonymous, "get")] HttpRequest req) =>
        new OkObjectResult("ok");
}
```

With managed identities, the `Connection` settings point to service endpoints
(`ServiceBus__fullyQualifiedNamespace`) rather than connection strings with keys.

## Hosting plans

| Plan | Scale to zero | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------|
| Flex Consumption | Yes | Recommended serverless plan; VNet integration; always-ready instances |
| Consumption | Yes | Legacy serverless plan; short default timeouts |
| Premium (Elastic) | No (pre-warmed) | No cold starts, VNet, longer runs |
| Dedicated (App Service) | No | Run on an existing App Service plan |
| Container Apps | Yes | Functions on the Container Apps platform |

## Durable Functions

```csharp
[Function(nameof(ProcessOrder))]
public static async Task ProcessOrder([OrchestrationTrigger] TaskOrchestrationContext context)
{
    var order = context.GetInput<Order>()!;
    await context.CallActivityAsync(nameof(ReserveStock), order);
    var paid = await context.CallActivityAsync<bool>(nameof(ChargeCard), order);
    if (!paid)
    {
        await context.CallActivityAsync(nameof(ReleaseStock), order);
        return;
    }
    await context.CallActivityAsync(nameof(ShipOrder), order);
}
```

Orchestrator code must be deterministic (no `DateTime.Now`, random numbers or direct I/O — use the
context's APIs and activities), because it is replayed from history.

## Design tips

- Keep functions small and idempotent; triggers can deliver messages more than once
- Put business logic in plain classes injected via DI, not in the function method
- Use Application Insights (OpenTelemetry) for distributed tracing across functions

## Choosing a container platform

| Service | Best for | You manage |
|---------|----------|------------|
| Container Instances (ACI) | Single containers, short jobs | Almost nothing |
| Container Apps (ACA) | Microservices, APIs, event-driven workers, jobs | Apps and scaling rules |
| AKS | Complex platforms needing full Kubernetes | Workloads, upgrades, node pools |
| App Service (containers) | Web apps packaged as containers | Very little |

## Build and push

```bash
az acr create -n acrshopprod -g rg-shop-prod --sku Standard
dotnet publish src/Shop.Api -c Release -t:PublishContainer \
  -p ContainerRegistry=acrshopprod.azurecr.io -p ContainerRepository=shop-api -p ContainerImageTag=1.4.0
```

(Run `az acr login -n acrshopprod` first so the SDK can push.)

## Deploy to Container Apps

```bash
az containerapp env create -n cae-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --location westeurope
az containerapp create -n ca-shop-api -g rg-shop-prod --environment cae-shop-prod \
  --image acrshopprod.azurecr.io/shop-api:1.4.0 \
  --registry-server acrshopprod.azurecr.io --registry-identity system \
  --target-port 8080 --ingress external \
  --min-replicas 0 --max-replicas 10
```

## Scaling with KEDA

Container Apps scale on HTTP concurrency, CPU, memory or event sources via KEDA scalers — for
example, the number of messages in a Service Bus queue. Workers can scale to zero when the queue
is empty and burst when messages arrive.

## Revisions and traffic splitting

Each deployment creates a **revision**. In multiple-revision mode you can send 10% of traffic to
the new revision, watch metrics, then shift the rest — canary releases without extra tooling.

## Container Apps jobs

Jobs run containers to completion on a schedule, on demand or in response to events — a good home
for batch tasks and migrations.

## Learning objectives

- Understand storage account services, tiers and redundancy
- Read and write blobs from .NET securely
- Optimise cost with lifecycle management

## Services in a storage account

| Service | Use |
|---------|-----|
| Blob Storage | Objects: documents, images, backups, data lake files (with hierarchical namespace = ADLS Gen2) |
| Azure Files | SMB/NFS file shares |
| Queue Storage | Simple message queues |
| Table Storage | Simple key/attribute NoSQL store |

## Access tiers

| Tier | Storage cost | Access cost | Minimum retention |
|------|--------------|-------------|-------------------|
| Hot | Highest | Lowest | — |
| Cool | Lower | Higher | 30 days |
| Cold | Lower still | Higher still | 90 days |
| Archive | Lowest | Highest; offline | 180 days |

## Redundancy

| Option | Copies |
|--------|--------|
| LRS | 3 copies in one datacenter |
| ZRS | 3 copies across zones in one region |
| GRS / RA-GRS | LRS + async copy to the paired region (RA = read access to the secondary) |
| GZRS / RA-GZRS | ZRS + async copy to the paired region |

## Blobs from .NET

```csharp
var container = blobs.GetBlobContainerClient("uploads");
await container.CreateIfNotExistsAsync(cancellationToken: ct);

var blob = container.GetBlobClient($"{userId}/{Guid.CreateVersion7()}.png");
await blob.UploadAsync(stream, new BlobUploadOptions
{
    HttpHeaders = new BlobHttpHeaders { ContentType = "image/png" }
}, ct);
```

## Letting clients upload directly

```csharp
var delegationKey = await blobs.GetUserDelegationKeyAsync(DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddMinutes(15), ct);

var sas = new BlobSasBuilder(BlobSasPermissions.Create | BlobSasPermissions.Write, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddMinutes(15))
{
    BlobContainerName = "uploads",
    BlobName = blobName
};

var uri = new BlobUriBuilder(blob.Uri)
{
    Sas = sas.ToSasQueryParameters(delegationKey, blobs.AccountName)
}.ToUri();
```

The browser uploads straight to storage with this short-lived URL; your API never handles the bytes.

## Lifecycle management

Policies move blobs to cooler tiers or delete them by age — for example, logs to Cool after 30
days, Archive after 180, delete after 7 years.

## The Azure SQL family

| Option | Model | Use when |
|--------|-------|----------|
| Azure SQL Database | PaaS, database-scoped | New cloud apps, SaaS, most workloads |
| Elastic pools | PaaS, shared resources | Many databases with varying usage (multi-tenant SaaS) |

|------|-----------------|

## Connecting from .NET

```csharp
builder.Services.AddDbContext<ShopDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(
```

```json
{
```

## Business continuity

- Automated backups with point-in-time restore (retention configurable, long-term retention optional)

  that follows the primary

## Security

- Private endpoints and disabled public network access
- Transparent Data Encryption (on by default), Always Encrypted for highly sensitive columns
- Microsoft Defender for SQL for threat detection and vulnerability assessment

  - id: ru
    prompt: Which statements about Request Units (RUs) are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: RUs normalise the cost of database operations (CPU, IOPS, memory) into one currency
        correct: true
      - text: A point read of a 1 KB item by ID and partition key costs about 1 RU
        correct: true
      - text: Cross-partition queries generally cost more than single-partition queries
        correct: true
      - text: Every operation costs exactly 1 RU regardless of size or complexity
    explanation: Model data and queries so most operations are point reads or single-partition queries.

## Learning objectives

- Understand Cosmos DB's APIs, partitioning and consistency
- Model data around access patterns
- Use the .NET SDK efficiently

## What Cosmos DB is

A globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database with single-digit-millisecond latency, automatic
indexing and multi-region replication. APIs include **NoSQL** (native), **MongoDB**, **Apache
Cassandra**, **Apache Gremlin** and **Table**.

## Partitioning

```text
Container "orders"  —  partition key: /customerId
  logical partition "c-1001": order-1, order-7, order-9
  logical partition "c-1002": order-2
  ...
```

- All items with the same key live in one **logical partition** (max 20 GB)
- Logical partitions are spread over **physical partitions** automatically
- Queries that include the partition key go to one partition; others fan out

## Consistency levels

| Level | Guarantee |
|-------|-----------|
| Strong | Linearizable reads |
| Bounded staleness | Reads lag by at most K versions or T time |
| **Session** (default) | Read your own writes, monotonic reads within a session |
| Consistent prefix | Never see out-of-order writes |
| Eventual | No ordering guarantee; lowest latency and cost |

## Throughput

- **Provisioned** (manual or autoscale) — RU/s reserved per container or database
- **Serverless** — pay per RU consumed; good for low or spiky traffic

## The .NET SDK

```csharp
var client = new CosmosClient("https://cosmos-shop-prod.documents.azure.com:443/", credential,
    new CosmosClientOptions { ApplicationName = "shop-api" });
var orders = client.GetContainer("shop", "orders");

await orders.UpsertItemAsync(order, new PartitionKey(order.CustomerId), cancellationToken: ct);

var response = await orders.ReadItemAsync<Order>(orderId, new PartitionKey(customerId), cancellationToken: ct);
Console.WriteLine($"Cost: {response.RequestCharge} RU");

var query = orders.GetItemQueryIterator<Order>(
    new QueryDefinition("SELECT * FROM o WHERE o.customerId = @c AND o.status = 'Open'").WithParameter("@c", customerId),
    requestOptions: new QueryRequestOptions { PartitionKey = new PartitionKey(customerId) });
```

Register `CosmosClient` as a **singleton** — it manages connections and should live for the app's
lifetime.

## Modelling tips

- Model for your queries; denormalise data that is read together
- Embed child items that are bounded (order lines); reference unbounded relationships
- Use the change feed to build materialized views and trigger downstream processing

        correct: true

        correct: true

    explanation: Event Grid is for reactive event distribution. Replayable streams are the job of Event Hubs.

## Learning objectives

- Distinguish messages from events
- Choose the right Azure messaging service
- Send and receive Service Bus messages from .NET

## Messages vs events

- A **message** is a command or data the sender expects someone to process ("charge this card")
- An **event** is a notification that something happened ("blob created"); the publisher doesn't
  care who reacts

## Choosing

| Service | Model | Use for |
|---------|-------|---------|
| **Service Bus** | Broker: queues and topics/subscriptions | Business workflows, commands, ordered and transactional processing |
| **Event Grid** | Push-based pub/sub of discrete events | Reacting to resource events and app events |
| **Event Hubs** | Partitioned streaming log | Telemetry, clickstreams, high-volume ingestion |
| **Storage Queues** | Simple queue | Basic, cheap, large backlogs, minimal features |

## Service Bus from .NET

```csharp
await using var client = new ServiceBusClient("sb-shop-prod.servicebus.windows.net", credential);

await using var sender = client.CreateSender("orders");
await sender.SendMessageAsync(new ServiceBusMessage(BinaryData.FromObjectAsJson(orderPlaced))
{
    MessageId = orderPlaced.OrderId.ToString(),   // enables duplicate detection
    SessionId = orderPlaced.CustomerId.ToString(),
    Subject = "OrderPlaced"
}, ct);
```

```csharp
await using var processor = client.CreateSessionProcessor("orders", new ServiceBusSessionProcessorOptions
{
    MaxConcurrentSessions = 8,
    AutoCompleteMessages = false
});

processor.ProcessMessageAsync += async args =>
{
    var evt = args.Message.Body.ToObjectFromJson<OrderPlaced>();
    await handler.HandleAsync(evt, args.CancellationToken);
    await args.CompleteMessageAsync(args.Message);
};
processor.ProcessErrorAsync += args => { logger.LogError(args.Exception, "Service Bus error"); return Task.CompletedTask; };

await processor.StartProcessingAsync(ct);
```

## Reliability patterns

- **Peek-lock** — a message is locked while processed; complete it on success, abandon it to retry
- **Dead-letter queue** — messages that exceed max delivery count go to a DLQ for inspection
- **Idempotent handlers** — at-least-once delivery means duplicates can happen
- **Outbox pattern** — write the message to your database in the same transaction as the state
  change, then publish, so you never lose or invent events

## Event Hubs basics

Producers send to partitions; consumer groups read independently, each tracking its position
(checkpoint) — like Kafka. Retention lets consumers replay; Capture writes events to storage
automatically.

## Learning objectives

- Design virtual networks and subnets
- Secure traffic with NSGs
- Reach PaaS services privately with private endpoints

## Virtual networks

A **VNet** is your private network in a region, with an address space (for example
`10.20.0.0/16`) divided into **subnets**:

```text
vnet-shop-prod (10.20.0.0/16)
├── snet-app        10.20.1.0/24   App Service VNet integration (delegated)
├── snet-private    10.20.2.0/24   Private endpoints (SQL, storage, Key Vault)
└── snet-aks        10.20.16.0/20  AKS nodes
```

VNets connect to each other with **peering**, and to on-premises networks with **VPN Gateway** or
**ExpressRoute**. A **NAT Gateway** gives subnets a stable outbound IP.

## Network security groups

```bash
az network nsg rule create -g rg-shop-prod --nsg-name nsg-private -n deny-internet-inbound \
  --priority 4000 --direction Inbound --access Deny --source-address-prefixes Internet --destination-port-ranges '*'
```

Rules are evaluated by priority (lowest number first). Service tags such as `AzureLoadBalancer`
or `Sql` keep rules readable.

## Private endpoints

```bash
az network private-endpoint create -g rg-shop-prod -n pe-sql-shop \
  --vnet-name vnet-shop-prod --subnet snet-private \
  --private-connection-resource-id $(az sql server show -n sql-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --query id -o tsv) \
  --group-id sqlServer --connection-name sql-shop
az sql server update -n sql-shop-prod -g rg-shop-prod --enable-public-network false
```

Link a private DNS zone (`privatelink.database.windows.net`) to the VNet so
`sql-shop-prod.database.windows.net` resolves to `10.20.2.x` from inside the network.

## Private endpoints vs service endpoints

| | Private endpoint | Service endpoint |
|-|------------------|------------------|
| Mechanism | Private IP for a specific resource in your VNet | Optimised route from a subnet to a service's public endpoint |
| Data exfiltration protection | Strong (scoped to one resource) | Weaker |
| On-premises access | Yes (via VPN/ExpressRoute) | No |
| Cost | Hourly + data charges | Free |

Private endpoints are the default recommendation for production data services.

## Learning objectives

- Choose the right load-balancing service
- Combine global and regional services

## The four options

| Service | Scope | Layer | Highlights |
|---------|-------|-------|------------|
| Azure Front Door | Global | 7 (HTTP/S) | Edge network, CDN caching, WAF, TLS offload, path routing, health probes |
| Traffic Manager | Global | DNS | Routes by priority, weight, performance or geography; any protocol |
| Application Gateway | Regional | 7 (HTTP/S) | Path/host routing, WAF, TLS termination, AKS ingress |
| Load Balancer | Regional | 4 (TCP/UDP) | Ultra-low latency, high throughput, internal or public |

## Decision guide

- Public web app or API, possibly multi-region → **Front Door**
- Regional web traffic that must stay inside a VNet with WAF → **Application Gateway**
- Non-HTTP traffic within a region → **Load Balancer**
- Non-HTTP global failover → **Traffic Manager**

## A typical multi-region web app

```text
Users ──▶ Front Door (WAF, caching)
            ├──▶ App Service (West Europe)  ──▶ Azure SQL failover group primary
            └──▶ App Service (North Europe) ──▶ Azure SQL failover group secondary
```

Front Door health probes route around a failed region automatically. Restrict the App Services to
accept traffic only from your Front Door profile (access restrictions with the `AzureFrontDoor.Backend`
service tag plus the `X-Azure-FDID` header check).

## Health endpoints

Every load balancer needs a meaningful health endpoint:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddCheck<DatabaseHealthCheck>("database", tags: ["ready"]);

app.MapHealthChecks("/healthz/live", new() { Predicate = _ => false });
app.MapHealthChecks("/healthz/ready", new() { Predicate = c => c.Tags.Contains("ready") });
```

Liveness says "the process works"; readiness says "I can serve traffic, dependencies included".

## Instrumenting an app

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().UseAzureMonitor();
```

With the `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` setting present, requests, dependencies (HTTP, SQL),
exceptions, logs and metrics flow to Application Insights. Custom `ActivitySource`s and `Meter`s
are picked up when added to the OpenTelemetry builder.

## Querying with KQL

```kusto
requests
| where timestamp > ago(24h)
| summarize count(), p95 = percentile(duration, 95), failures = countif(success == false) by name
| order by failures desc
```

```kusto
exceptions
| where timestamp > ago(1h)
| summarize count() by type, outerMessage
| top 10 by count_
```

## Platform logs

Resources emit metrics automatically; send their **resource logs** (for example SQL query stats,
Key Vault access, Front Door access logs) to a Log Analytics workspace with **diagnostic settings**.

## Alerting

| Alert type | Example |
|------------|---------|
| Metric | CPU > 80% for 10 minutes on the App Service plan |
| Log search | More than 20 failed requests to `/checkout` in 5 minutes |
| Activity log | Someone deleted a resource group |
| Smart detection | Unusual rise in failure rate |

Route alerts through **action groups** (e-mail, SMS, Teams, webhooks, Logic Apps). Alert on symptoms
users feel — errors and latency — rather than on every internal metric.

## Distributed tracing

Application Insights' **application map** and **transaction search** show a request flowing across
App Service, Functions, Service Bus and SQL, because W3C trace context propagates automatically
through instrumented clients.

      - text: It uses templates that combine app code, Bicep or Terraform, and an `azure.yaml` file
        correct: true
      - text: It can set up a CI/CD pipeline with `azd pipeline config`
        correct: true
      - text: It only works with Java applications
    explanation: "`azd` works with .NET, Node.js, Python, Java and more."
---
## Learning objectives

- Declare Azure resources with Bicep
- Preview and deploy changes safely
- Use `azd` for an end-to-end developer workflow

## A Bicep file

```bicep
param location string = resourceGroup().location
param env string
var suffix = '${env}-${uniqueString(resourceGroup().id)}'

resource plan 'Microsoft.Web/serverfarms@2024-04-01' = {
  name: 'asp-shop-${suffix}'
  location: location
  sku: { name: 'P1v3', capacity: 2 }
  kind: 'linux'
  properties: { reserved: true }
}

resource app 'Microsoft.Web/sites@2024-04-01' = {
  name: 'app-shop-${suffix}'
  location: location
  identity: { type: 'SystemAssigned' }
  properties: {
    serverFarmId: plan.id
    httpsOnly: true
    siteConfig: {
      linuxFxVersion: 'DOTNETCORE|10.0'
      healthCheckPath: '/healthz/ready'
      minTlsVersion: '1.2'
    }
  }
}

output appPrincipalId string = app.identity.principalId
```

## Deploying

```bash
az deployment group what-if -g rg-shop-prod -f main.bicep -p env=prod
az deployment group create  -g rg-shop-prod -f main.bicep -p env=prod
```

Deployments are **declarative and idempotent**: running the same template twice makes no changes.

## Modules

```bicep
module sql 'modules/sql.bicep' = {
  name: 'sql'
  params: { location: location, env: env, adminGroupObjectId: adminGroupId }
}
```

Modules (local or from a Bicep registry) keep templates small and reusable. **Azure Verified
Modules** provide Microsoft-maintained building blocks.

## Azure Developer CLI

```bash
azd init --template todo-csharp-sql
azd up            # provision + deploy
azd deploy        # code only
azd down          # tear everything down
```

## Terraform

Terraform with the `azurerm` provider is a popular alternative, especially for multi-cloud teams.
Whatever the tool, the principles are the same: everything in Git, changes through pull requests,
previews before applies, and no manual portal changes in production.

## Learning objectives

- Enforce standards with Azure Policy
- Protect critical resources with locks
- Monitor and optimise cost

## Azure Policy

```json
{
  "if": {
    "allOf": [
      { "field": "type", "equals": "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts" },
      { "field": "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/allowBlobPublicAccess", "equals": true }
    ]
  },
  "then": { "effect": "deny" }
}
```

| Effect | Behaviour |
|--------|-----------|
| `audit` / `auditIfNotExists` | Report non-compliance |
| `deny` | Block non-compliant requests |
| `modify` / `append` | Change properties (e.g. add tags) |
| `deployIfNotExists` | Deploy a related resource (e.g. diagnostic settings) |

Group policies into **initiatives** (for example, the *Microsoft cloud security benchmark*) and
assign them at management group scope so every subscription inherits them.

## Locks

```bash
az lock create --name protect-prod-sql --lock-type CanNotDelete \
  --resource-group rg-shop-prod --resource-name sql-shop-prod --resource-type Microsoft.Sql/servers
```

## Landing zones

The **Cloud Adoption Framework** describes landing zones: a pre-configured hierarchy of
management groups, subscriptions, networking, identity and policies into which application teams
deploy. It turns governance from a review meeting into guardrails.

## Cost management

- **Cost analysis** — break down spend by subscription, resource group, service and tag
- **Budgets** — alerts at thresholds such as 80% and 100% of a monthly amount
- **Advisor** — right-sizing and idle resource recommendations
- **Reservations and savings plans** — discounts for one- or three-year commitments
- **Azure Hybrid Benefit** — reuse existing Windows Server and SQL Server licences
- **Dev/test pricing** and auto-shutdown for non-production resources

```bash
az consumption budget create --budget-name shop-prod-monthly --amount 5000 \
  --category cost --time-grain monthly --start-date 2026-11-01 --end-date 2027-10-31 \
  --resource-group rg-shop-prod
```

Make cost a non-functional requirement reviewed like performance and security.

title: One component model, many hosts
questions:
  - id: what-is

    explanation: Razor components are the unit of UI. Where and how they run — server, browser or native app — is a hosting decision.
  - id: hybrid

    options:
      - text: In WebAssembly inside the embedded web view
      - id: native
        text: Natively in the app's .NET process, rendering into an embedded web view
        correct: true
      - text: On a remote web server
    explanation: Hybrid components run on the device's .NET runtime with full native API access; the `BlazorWebView` only displays the HTML.
  - id: hosts
    prompt: Which are real ways to host Blazor components?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: A Blazor Web App served by ASP.NET Core, with static and interactive render modes
        correct: true
      - text: A standalone Blazor WebAssembly app served as static files
        correct: true
      - text: A .NET MAUI, WPF or Windows Forms app using `BlazorWebView`
        correct: true
      - text: Directly inside SQL Server stored procedures
    explanation: Blazor Web App, standalone WebAssembly and Hybrid are the three hosting families.
---
Blazor is not one technology but one **component model** that runs in several places.

## Learning objectives

- Describe the Blazor hosting families
- Explain where component code runs in each model
- Choose a starting point for a new project

## Razor components

```razor
<h3>@Title</h3>
<button class="btn" @onclick="() => count++">Clicked @count times</button>

@code {
    [Parameter] public string Title { get; set; } = "Counter";
    private int count;
}
```

The same component can be rendered as static HTML on the server, run interactively on the server
over a real-time connection, run in the browser on WebAssembly, or run inside a native desktop or
mobile app.

## The hosting families

| Family | Code runs | Typical use |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| **Blazor Web App** | Server, browser, or both — chosen per component by render mode | Most new web apps |
| **Standalone WebAssembly** | Browser only; host is any static file server | Offline-capable SPAs, GitHub Pages, CDNs |
| **Blazor Hybrid** | Natively on the device, displayed in a `BlazorWebView` | Desktop and mobile apps sharing web UI |

Before .NET 8, people spoke of "Blazor Server" and "Blazor WebAssembly" as separate project types.
Since .NET 8, the **Blazor Web App** template unifies them: one app, with each page or component
choosing how it renders.

## Choosing a starting point

- Public content site with some interactivity → Blazor Web App, static SSR by default
- Internal line-of-business app on a fast network → Blazor Web App with Interactive Server
- App that must work offline or be hosted purely as static files → standalone WebAssembly
- Desktop/mobile app with shared UI → Hybrid, with components in a shared Razor class library

> This site is itself a standalone Blazor WebAssembly app hosted on GitHub Pages.

title: Render modes
questions:
  - id: static-ssr
    prompt: A component with no render mode in a Blazor Web App renders with static server-side rendering. What does that mean?
    options:
      - id: html-only
        text: The server renders HTML once per request; `@onclick` handlers do not run
        correct: true
      - text: It runs in WebAssembly after the page loads
      - text: It keeps a SignalR circuit open
      - text: It cannot use any C# code
    explanation: Static SSR produces plain HTML. Interactivity requires an interactive render mode; forms and links can still work through enhanced navigation and form posts.
  - id: auto
    prompt: How does the `InteractiveAuto` render mode decide how to run a component?
    options:
      - text: It always uses WebAssembly
      - id: auto-choice
        text: It uses Interactive Server while the WebAssembly runtime is not yet available, and WebAssembly once it can be loaded quickly
        correct: true
      - text: It asks the user to choose
      - text: It switches back and forth on every click
    explanation: Auto gives fast first interaction via the server, then moves to client-side execution on later visits once assets are cached. A component keeps its chosen mode once it starts.
  - id: prerender
    prompt: How do you disable prerendering for an interactive server component?
    options:
      - text: Add `@prerender false` to the component
      - text: Prerendering cannot be disabled
      - id: new-mode
        text: "`@rendermode @(new InteractiveServerRenderMode(prerender: false))`"
        correct: true
    explanation: Each interactive render mode class takes a `prerender` argument; prerendering is on by default.
  - id: rules
    prompt: Which statements about render modes are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: Interactive WebAssembly and Auto components must be in an assembly the browser can download, usually the `.Client` project
        correct: true
      - text: Parameters passed from a static parent to an interactive child must be serializable
        correct: true
      - text: A child of an interactive component inherits its parent's render mode
        correct: true
      - text: A child of an Interactive Server component can switch itself to Interactive WebAssembly
    explanation: Render mode flows down the tree and cannot be switched to a different interactive mode inside an interactive subtree.
---
## Learning objectives

- Describe the four render modes
- Apply render modes per component, per page or globally
- Understand prerendering and the rules for mixing modes

## The four modes

| Mode | Where it runs | Interactive | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------------|-------|
| Static SSR | Server, per request | No | Fast, SEO-friendly HTML |
| `InteractiveServer` | Server, over a SignalR circuit | Yes | Tiny download; needs a constant connection |
| `InteractiveWebAssembly` | Browser | Yes | Works offline after download; larger first load |
| `InteractiveAuto` | Server first, then browser | Yes | Best of both, more moving parts |

## Applying a render mode

```razor
@page "/counter"
@rendermode InteractiveServer
```

```razor
<Counter @rendermode="InteractiveWebAssembly" />
```

Make an entire app interactive by setting the mode on the root `Routes` and `HeadOutlet`
components in `App.razor`:

```razor
<HeadOutlet @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
<Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
```

## Prerendering

Interactive components are **prerendered** on the server by default: the user sees HTML
immediately, then the component becomes interactive. Lifecycle methods therefore run twice — once
during prerender and once when interactive — which matters for data loading (see the state
chapter).

## Knowing where you are

.NET 9 added `RendererInfo` and `AssignedRenderMode`:

```razor
@if (!RendererInfo.IsInteractive)
{
    <p>Loading interactive features…</p>
}
<button disabled="@(!RendererInfo.IsInteractive)" @onclick="Save">Save</button>

<small>Running on: @RendererInfo.Name</small>
```

`RendererInfo.Name` is `Static`, `Server`, `WebAssembly` or `WebView`. Disabling buttons until
interactive prevents clicks that would do nothing during prerendering.

## Rules for mixing modes

- Interactive modes flow **down** the component tree
- A child cannot switch to a *different* interactive mode
- Parameters from a static parent to an interactive child must be JSON-serializable — so you
  cannot pass `RenderFragment` child content across that boundary
- WebAssembly/Auto components must live where the browser can download them

## Learning objectives

- Create a Blazor Web App from the template
- Understand the server and client projects
- Read the `Program.cs` that wires render modes together

## Creating the app

```bash
dotnet new blazor -n Shop --interactivity Auto
```

| Option | Values |
|--------|--------|
| `--interactivity` | `None`, `Server`, `WebAssembly`, `Auto` |
| `--all-interactive` | Make the whole app interactive instead of per page |
| `--auth` | `None` or `Individual` |

## Solution layout

```text
Shop/                    server project (ASP.NET Core)
  Components/
    App.razor            root HTML document
    Routes.razor         router
    Layout/
    Pages/               static or server-interactive pages
  Program.cs
Shop.Client/             WebAssembly project
  Pages/                 pages that can run in the browser
  Program.cs
```

## Server Program.cs

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddRazorComponents()
    .AddInteractiveServerComponents()
    .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents();

var app = builder.Build();

app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseAntiforgery();
app.MapStaticAssets();

app.MapRazorComponents<App>()
    .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode()
    .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode()
    .AddAdditionalAssemblies(typeof(Shop.Client._Imports).Assembly);

app.Run();
```

`MapStaticAssets` (.NET 9+) serves static files with build-time compression and fingerprinting.

## Client Program.cs

```csharp
var builder = WebAssemblyHostBuilder.CreateDefault(args);
builder.Services.AddScoped<ICartService, ClientCartService>();
await builder.Build().RunAsync();
```

Services used by components that may run in **both** places must be registered in **both**
`Program.cs` files — often with different implementations. That idea is the key to reusable
Blazor components and is covered in the data chapter.

## _Imports.razor

```razor
@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web
@using static Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.RenderMode
```

The static import is what lets you write `@rendermode InteractiveServer` instead of
`RenderMode.InteractiveServer`.

## Learning objectives

- Read and write Razor component syntax
- Split markup and code with partial classes
- Inject services and use common directives

## Anatomy

```razor
@page "/orders/{Id:int}"
@inject IOrderService Orders
@implements IDisposable

<PageTitle>Order @Id</PageTitle>

@if (order is null)
{
    <p>Loading…</p>
}
else
{
    <h1>Order @order.Number</h1>
    <ul>
        @foreach (var line in order.Lines)
        {
            <li @key="line.Sku">@line.Quantity × @line.Name</li>
        }
    </ul>
}

@code {
    [Parameter] public int Id { get; set; }
    private OrderDetails? order;

    protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync() => order = await Orders.GetAsync(Id);

    public void Dispose() { }
}
```

## Common directives

| Directive | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `@page` | Route template |
| `@rendermode` | Render mode for this component |
| `@inject` | Inject a service |
| `@using` / `@namespace` | Namespaces |
| `@implements` / `@inherits` | Interfaces and base class |
| `@typeparam` | Generic component type parameter |
| `@attribute` | Apply a C# attribute, e.g. `[Authorize]` |
| `@layout` | Choose a layout |

## Code-behind

```csharp
// OrderPage.razor.cs
public partial class OrderPage(IOrderService orders)
{
    [Parameter] public int Id { get; set; }
    private OrderDetails? order;

    protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync() => order = await orders.GetAsync(Id);
}
```

Constructor injection in components is supported from .NET 9. Code-behind keeps large components
navigable and lets you unit test logic more easily.

## Razor expressions

- `@value` — implicit expression; HTML-encoded output
- `@(a + b)` — explicit expression
- `@((MarkupString)html)` — render trusted raw HTML (never untrusted input)
- `@* comment *@` — Razor comment, not sent to the browser

title: Parameters, events and data binding
questions:
  - id: eventcallback
    prompt: Why should child components expose events as `EventCallback` rather than `Action`?
    options:
      - id: rerender
        text: "`EventCallback` invokes the handler on the right component and automatically re-renders the parent afterwards, and supports async handlers"
        correct: true
      - text: "`Action` cannot be used in Razor files"
      - text: "`EventCallback` is faster because it uses reflection"
    explanation: With a plain `Action`, the parent's state changes but it does not know to re-render.
  - id: two-way
    prompt: To support `@bind-Value` on a custom component, which members must it expose?
    options:
      - text: Only a `[Parameter] public string Value { get; set; }`
      - text: "A `[Parameter] public string Bind { get; set; }`"
      - id: value-changed
        text: A `[Parameter] Value` property and a `[Parameter] EventCallback<T> ValueChanged`
        correct: true
    explanation: "`@bind-Value` expands to setting `Value` and handling `ValueChanged`. An optional `ValueExpression` supports validation in forms."
  - id: dont-mutate
    prompt: Why should a component avoid writing to its own `[Parameter]` properties?
    options:
      - text: It causes a compile error
      - text: Parameters are read-only at runtime
      - id: overwritten
        text: The parent may re-render and overwrite the value, discarding the child's changes
        correct: true
    explanation: Parameters are owned by the parent. Copy into private state or raise an event so the parent updates the value.
  - id: bind-modifiers
    prompt: Which binding features are available in Blazor?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: "`@bind:event=\"oninput\"` to update on every keystroke"
        correct: true
      - text: "`@bind:after` to run a method after the bound value changes"
        correct: true
      - text: "`@bind:get` and `@bind:set` to separate reading and writing the value"
        correct: true
      - text: "`@bind:sql` to save the value directly to a database"
    explanation: Bind modifiers customise when and how binding happens.
---
## Learning objectives

- Pass data down with parameters
- Raise events up with `EventCallback`
- Implement two-way binding on your own components

## Parameters

```razor
@* Rating.razor *@
<div class="rating" aria-label="@Value out of @Max stars">
    @for (var i = 1; i <= Max; i++)
    {
        var star = i;
        <button type="button" class="@(star <= Value ? "on" : "off")" @onclick="() => SelectAsync(star)">★</button>
    }
</div>

@code {
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public int Value { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public EventCallback<int> ValueChanged { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public int Max { get; set; } = 5;

    private Task SelectAsync(int star) => ValueChanged.InvokeAsync(star);
}
```

`[EditorRequired]` makes the compiler warn when a parent forgets the parameter. Note the `var star = i;`
copy: the lambda must capture the loop value, not the loop variable.

## Two-way binding

```razor
<Rating @bind-Value="review.Stars" />
<p>You chose @review.Stars stars.</p>
```

`@bind-Value` expands to `Value="review.Stars"` plus `ValueChanged="v => review.Stars = v"`.

## Binding to inputs

```razor
<input @bind="search" @bind:event="oninput" @bind:after="SearchAsync" />

<input @bind:get="quantity" @bind:set="SetQuantity" type="number" />

@code {
    private string search = "";
    private int quantity = 1;

    private Task SearchAsync() => results.LoadAsync(search);
    private void SetQuantity(int value) => quantity = Math.Clamp(value, 1, 99);
}
```

## Events

```razor
<button @onclick="SaveAsync" @onclick:preventDefault>Save</button>
<input @onkeydown="OnKeyDown" />

@code {
    private async Task SaveAsync(MouseEventArgs e) { /* ... */ }
    private void OnKeyDown(KeyboardEventArgs e)
    {
        if (e.Key == "Escape") Close();
    }
}
```

Handlers can be sync or async. After an event handler completes, Blazor re-renders the component
automatically; for async handlers it renders once when the first `await` yields and again when it finishes.

title: Lifecycle and rendering
questions:
  - id: order
    prompt: In which order do these lifecycle methods first run for a new component?
    options:

      - text: OnParametersSet, SetParametersAsync, OnInitialized, OnAfterRender

      - id: external
        text: When state changes outside Blazor's own event handling, such as from a timer or a service event
        correct: true
    explanation: Blazor re-renders after its own events and lifecycle methods. For external triggers, call `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`.
  - id: key
    prompt: What does the `@key` directive do in a list?
    options:
      - id: identity
        text: Tells the diffing algorithm which rendered element or component corresponds to which data item, preserving them correctly when the list changes
        correct: true
      - text: Encrypts the element
      - text: Sets the HTML `id` attribute
    explanation: Without `@key`, Blazor matches by position, which can reuse the wrong component instance (and its state) after inserts or reorders.
  - id: render-facts
    prompt: Which statements about Blazor rendering are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: Blazor builds a render tree and applies only the differences to the DOM
        correct: true
      - text: Overriding `ShouldRender` to return false can skip unnecessary renders
        correct: true
      - text: "`OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)` is the right place to call JavaScript that needs rendered elements"
        correct: true
      - text: "`OnAfterRender` runs during static server-side rendering"
    explanation: After-render callbacks only run for interactive components, because static SSR has no live DOM on the server.
---
## Learning objectives

- Know the order and purpose of lifecycle methods
- Trigger re-renders correctly
- Use `@key` and `ShouldRender` to control rendering

## The lifecycle

1. `SetParametersAsync` — parameters arrive
2. `OnInitialized{Async}` — first time only
3. `OnParametersSet{Async}` — first time and whenever the parent passes new parameters
4. Render
5. `OnAfterRender{Async}(firstRender)` — DOM updated (interactive only)
6. `Dispose` / `DisposeAsync` — removed from the tree

```razor
@implements IAsyncDisposable
@inject IJSRuntime JS

<div @ref="chartHost"></div>

@code {
    [Parameter] public IReadOnlyList<Point> Data { get; set; } = [];
    private ElementReference chartHost;
    private IJSObjectReference? module;

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            module = await JS.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", "./Components/Chart.razor.js");
        }
        if (module is not null)
        {
            await module.InvokeVoidAsync("draw", chartHost, Data);
        }
    }

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        if (module is not null)
        {
            try { await module.DisposeAsync(); } catch (JSDisconnectedException) { }
        }
    }
}
```

## Re-rendering from outside

```csharp
protected override void OnInitialized() => cart.Changed += OnCartChanged;

private void OnCartChanged() => _ = InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);

public void Dispose() => cart.Changed -= OnCartChanged;
```

`InvokeAsync` marshals onto the renderer's synchronization context — essential in Interactive
Server, where the event may arrive on another thread. Always unsubscribe to avoid memory leaks.

## Diffing and @key

```razor
@foreach (var todo in todos)
{
    <TodoItem @key="todo.Id" Item="todo" />
}
```

## Skipping renders

```csharp
private int lastVersion = -1;

protected override bool ShouldRender()
{
    var changed = Data.Version != lastVersion;
    lastVersion = Data.Version;
    return changed;
}
```

Use `ShouldRender` only for measured hot spots; most components render quickly enough.

title: Templated and generic components
questions:
  - id: childcontent
    prompt: What is special about a parameter named `ChildContent` of type `RenderFragment`?
    options:

        text: Markup placed between the component's opening and closing tags is assigned to it automatically
        correct: true
      - text: It must be set in code, never in markup
      - text: It is rendered before the component's own markup
      - text: It can only contain plain text

  - id: render-fragment-t
    prompt: What does `RenderFragment<TItem>` allow?
    options:
      - text: Rendering only items of type `string`
      - id: template
        text: A template that receives a value — for example, how to render each row of a list
        correct: true
      - text: Running a fragment on a background thread
    explanation: The caller supplies markup that uses `context` (or a named `Context`) to access the item.
  - id: typeparam
    prompt: Which statements about generic components are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: "`@typeparam TItem` declares a type parameter"
        correct: true
      - text: The type argument can often be inferred from a parameter such as `Items`
        correct: true
      - text: "Constraints can be added, for example `@typeparam TItem where TItem : notnull`"
        correct: true

    explanation: Generic components and render fragments combine to build reusable grids, lists and pickers.

Reusable components separate **what** to render (the caller's business) from **how** to lay it
out (the component's business).

## Learning objectives

- Accept child content with `RenderFragment`
- Accept item templates with `RenderFragment<T>`
- Build generic components with `@typeparam`

## Child content

```razor
@* Card.razor *@
<section class="card">
    <header>@Header</header>
    <div class="card-body">@ChildContent</div>
</section>

@code {
    [Parameter] public RenderFragment? Header { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public RenderFragment? ChildContent { get; set; }
}
```

```razor
<Card>
    <Header><h2>Shipping</h2></Header>
    <ChildContent><p>Arrives in 2–3 days.</p></ChildContent>
</Card>

<Card>
    <p>Only child content — no tag needed.</p>
</Card>
```

## A generic, templated list

```razor
@* ItemList.razor *@
@typeparam TItem where TItem : notnull

@if (Items.Count == 0)
{
    @Empty
}
else
{
    <ul class="item-list">
        @foreach (var item in Items)
        {
            <li @key="item">@ItemTemplate(item)</li>
        }
    </ul>
}

@code {
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public IReadOnlyList<TItem> Items { get; set; } = [];
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public RenderFragment<TItem> ItemTemplate { get; set; } = default!;
    [Parameter] public RenderFragment Empty { get; set; } = @<p>Nothing here yet.</p>;
}
```

```razor
<ItemList Items="products" Context="product">
    <ItemTemplate>
        <strong>@product.Name</strong> — @product.Price.ToString("C")
    </ItemTemplate>
</ItemList>
```

`TItem` is inferred as `Product` from `Items`. `Context="product"` renames the implicit `context`
variable. The same `ItemList` now renders customers, orders or anything else.

## Fragments in C#

```csharp
private RenderFragment Badge(string text) => @<span class="badge">@text</span>;
```

Razor templates (`@<tag>...</tag>`) can be written inline in `@code` blocks to produce fragments.

title: Cascading values and shared state
questions:
  - id: cascading
    prompt: What does a `CascadingValue` provide?
    options:
      - text: A value that is stored in the browser's local storage
      - text: A global static variable shared by all users
      - id: descendants
        text: A value available to every descendant component that declares a matching `[CascadingParameter]`
        correct: true
      - text: A CSS variable
    explanation: Cascading values avoid passing the same parameter through every level of the tree.
  - id: isfixed
    prompt: "What does `IsFixed=\"true\"` on a `CascadingValue` do?"
    options:
      - id: no-tracking
        text: Promises the value never changes, so Blazor skips change-notification subscriptions for better performance
        correct: true
      - text: Makes the value read-only for descendants
      - text: Pins the component to the top of the page
    explanation: Fixed cascading values are cheaper because descendants are not re-rendered when the cascading component re-renders.
  - id: state-container
    prompt: Which statements about a scoped "state container" service are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: In Interactive Server, a scoped service lives for the user's circuit
        correct: true
      - text: In WebAssembly, a scoped service effectively lives for the lifetime of the browser tab's app
        correct: true
      - text: Components should subscribe to its change event and unsubscribe when disposed
        correct: true
      - text: A singleton state container in Interactive Server is a safe place for per-user data
    explanation: Singletons on the server are shared by every user, so they must never hold per-user state.
---
## Learning objectives

- Share values down the tree with cascading values
- Register root-level cascading values
- Share state across components with a state container service

## Cascading values

```razor
<CascadingValue Value="theme" IsFixed="true">
    @Body
</CascadingValue>
```

```razor
@code {
    [CascadingParameter] public Theme Theme { get; set; } = default!;
}
```

Since .NET 8, cascading values can be registered at the root, which works across render-mode
boundaries where a `CascadingValue` component in a static layout could not reach:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddCascadingValue(sp => new Theme { Accent = "teal" });
builder.Services.AddCascadingAuthenticationState();
```

## A state container

```csharp
public sealed class CartState
{
    private readonly List<CartLine> _lines = [];
    public IReadOnlyList<CartLine> Lines => _lines;
    public decimal Total => _lines.Sum(l => l.Price * l.Quantity);
    public event Action? Changed;

    public void Add(Product product)
    {
        var line = _lines.FirstOrDefault(l => l.Sku == product.Sku);
        if (line is null) _lines.Add(new CartLine(product.Sku, product.Name, product.Price, 1));
        else line.Quantity++;
        Changed?.Invoke();
    }
}

builder.Services.AddScoped<CartState>();
```

```razor
@implements IDisposable
@inject CartState Cart

<span class="cart-badge">@Cart.Lines.Count</span>

@code {
    protected override void OnInitialized() => Cart.Changed += OnChanged;
    private void OnChanged() => InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);
    public void Dispose() => Cart.Changed -= OnChanged;
}
```

## Where the state lives

| Host | Scoped service lifetime |
|------|-------------------------|
| Interactive Server | The user's circuit |
| WebAssembly | The app instance in that browser tab |
| Static SSR | A single HTTP request |

State in memory disappears on refresh. Persist anything important — to the server through an API,
or to browser storage (see the interop section).

title: Razor class libraries, CSS isolation and attribute splatting

    options:
      - id: content

      - text: "`/logo.svg`"

  - id: css-isolation
    prompt: Which statements about CSS isolation are true?
    type: multiple
    options:

      - text: Isolated styles are bundled into a `{AssemblyName}.styles.css` file

  - id: splatting

    options:
      - id: splat
        text: Collecting any extra attributes the caller sets, so they can be applied to an element with `@attributes`
        correct: true

---
## Learning objectives

- Build a reusable component library
- Style components with CSS isolation
- Pass through arbitrary attributes with splatting

## Creating a library

```bash
dotnet new razorclasslib -n Contoso.UI
dotnet add Shop reference Contoso.UI
```

Add `@using Contoso.UI` to `_Imports.razor` and the components are available everywhere.

## A design-system button

```razor
@* Contoso.UI/Button.razor *@
<button type="@Type" class="cx-btn cx-btn-@Variant @Class" @attributes="AdditionalAttributes" @onclick="OnClick">
    @ChildContent
</button>

@code {
    [Parameter] public string Variant { get; set; } = "primary";
    [Parameter] public string Type { get; set; } = "button";
    [Parameter] public string? Class { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public RenderFragment? ChildContent { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public EventCallback<MouseEventArgs> OnClick { get; set; }
    [Parameter(CaptureUnmatchedValues = true)] public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object>? AdditionalAttributes { get; set; }
}
```

```razor
<Button Variant="danger" aria-label="Delete order" title="Delete" OnClick="DeleteAsync">Delete</Button>
```

`aria-label` and `title` are not parameters, so they land in `AdditionalAttributes` and are splatted
onto the `<button>`.

## CSS isolation

```css
/* Button.razor.css */
.cx-btn { border-radius: .5rem; padding: .5rem 1rem; }
.cx-btn-danger { background: #b91c1c; color: white; }
```

At build time, selectors are rewritten with a unique attribute such as `b-3xxtam6d07`, and all
isolated CSS is bundled into `Contoso.UI.bundle.scp.css`, which flows into the consuming app's
`{AssemblyName}.styles.css`. Reference it once in `App.razor`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="@Assets["Shop.styles.css"]" />
```

Use `::deep` to style child components from a parent:

```css
.card ::deep h2 { margin-top: 0; }
```

## Static assets

Files in the library's `wwwroot` are served from `_content/Contoso.UI/...`:

```html
<img src="_content/Contoso.UI/logo.svg" alt="Contoso" />
```

## Reuse across hosts

Keep RCL components free of host-specific services. Depend on interfaces (`IProductService`) that
each host implements, and the same library works in a Blazor Web App, standalone WebAssembly and a
MAUI Hybrid app.

---
title: Dynamic components and error boundaries
questions:
  - id: dynamic
    prompt: When is `DynamicComponent` useful?
    options:
      - text: To render components faster
      - id: runtime-type
        text: When the component type is only known at runtime, for example from configuration or a CMS
        correct: true
      - text: To load components from JavaScript
      - text: To generate components from SQL tables
    explanation: "`DynamicComponent` takes a `Type` and a `Parameters` dictionary and renders that component."
  - id: boundary
    prompt: What does an `ErrorBoundary` do?
    options:
      - text: Prevents all exceptions in the app, including in background services
      - text: Logs exceptions to the browser console only
      - id: contain
        text: Catches unhandled exceptions thrown while rendering its child content and shows fallback UI instead of breaking the whole app
        correct: true
    explanation: Error boundaries contain rendering and lifecycle failures in a subtree. In Interactive Server, an unhandled exception without a boundary terminates the circuit.
  - id: recover
    prompt: How do you let users retry after an `ErrorBoundary` shows its error content?
    options:
      - text: Reload the page; there is no other way
      - id: recover-method
        text: Call the boundary's `Recover()` method, for example from a button or when navigating
        correct: true
      - text: Set `IsFixed` to false
    explanation: "`Recover()` resets the boundary and re-renders its child content."
---
## Learning objectives

- Render components chosen at runtime
- Contain failures with error boundaries

## DynamicComponent

```razor
@foreach (var widget in dashboard.Widgets)
{
    <DynamicComponent Type="@WidgetTypes[widget.Kind]" Parameters="@widget.Settings" />
}

@code {
    private static readonly Dictionary<string, Type> WidgetTypes = new()
    {
        ["sales"] = typeof(SalesChart),
        ["tasks"] = typeof(TaskList),
        ["weather"] = typeof(WeatherCard)
    };
}
```

`Parameters` is an `IDictionary<string, object>` whose keys must match the target component's
parameter names. Map from configuration through an allow-list like the dictionary above; never
resolve arbitrary type names from user input.

## Error boundaries

```razor
<ErrorBoundary @ref="boundary">
    <ChildContent>
        <OrderHistory CustomerId="customerId" />
    </ChildContent>
    <ErrorContent Context="ex">
        <div class="alert">
            <p>We couldn't load your orders.</p>
            <button @onclick="() => boundary?.Recover()">Try again</button>
        </div>
    </ErrorContent>
</ErrorBoundary>

@code {
    private ErrorBoundary? boundary;
}
```

Put boundaries around independent regions — a widget, a panel — so one failure does not take
down the page. A common pattern is a boundary in the main layout that calls `Recover()` whenever
the route changes:

```csharp
protected override void OnParametersSet() => boundary?.Recover();
```

## What boundaries do not catch

Exceptions in event handlers you `await` inside the component are caught, but exceptions in
fire-and-forget tasks, timers or background services are not. Handle those explicitly and log them.

## Learning objectives

- Build forms with `EditForm` and input components
- Validate with DataAnnotations
- Customise validation and keep it secure

## A complete form

```csharp
public sealed class SignupModel
{
    [Required, EmailAddress]
    public string Email { get; set; } = "";

    [Required, StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 12, ErrorMessage = "Use at least 12 characters.")]
    public string Password { get; set; } = "";

    [Range(typeof(bool), "true", "true", ErrorMessage = "Please accept the terms.")]
    public bool AcceptTerms { get; set; }
}
```

```razor
<EditForm Model="model" OnValidSubmit="SubmitAsync">
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
    <ValidationSummary />

    <label>
        E-mail
        <InputText @bind-Value="model.Email" type="email" autocomplete="email" />
    </label>
    <ValidationMessage For="() => model.Email" />

    <label>
        Password
        <InputText @bind-Value="model.Password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" />
    </label>
    <ValidationMessage For="() => model.Password" />

    <label><InputCheckbox @bind-Value="model.AcceptTerms" /> I accept the terms</label>

    <button type="submit" disabled="@busy">Sign up</button>
</EditForm>

@code {
    private readonly SignupModel model = new();
    private bool busy;

    private async Task SubmitAsync()
    {
        busy = true;
        try { await Accounts.SignupAsync(model); }
        finally { busy = false; }
    }
}
```

## EditContext

`EditForm` creates an `EditContext` that tracks field changes and validation messages. Use it
directly for advanced scenarios:

```csharp
private EditContext? editContext;
protected override void OnInitialized() => editContext = new EditContext(model);
private bool CanSubmit => editContext?.IsModified() == true && editContext.GetValidationMessages().Any() == false;
```

## Custom validation

Implement `IValidatableObject` for cross-field rules, or a `ValidationAttribute` for reusable rules.
For complex rule sets, libraries such as FluentValidation integrate through a custom validator
component that adds messages to a `ValidationMessageStore`.

## Security reminder

In WebAssembly and Auto apps, component code is downloaded to the browser and can be modified.
Always validate again on the server — sharing the same model class between client and API makes
that cheap.

FILE: content/books/modern-blazor/04-forms-and-validation/02-forms-with-static-ssr.md

---
title: Forms with static server rendering
questions:
  - id: formname
    prompt: Why does an `EditForm` in a statically rendered component need a `FormName`?
    options:
      - text: It sets the HTML `<title>`
      - text: It is required for client-side validation only
      - text: It names the database table to save to
      - id: identify
        text: It identifies which form handler should process the POST, because several forms may exist on a page
        correct: true
    explanation: Static SSR forms post back to the server, and `FormName` routes the submission to the right component.
  - id: supply
    prompt: How does a static SSR component receive posted form values?
    options:
      - text: Through `[Parameter]` properties set by the parent
      - id: supply-from-form
        text: Through a property marked `[SupplyParameterFromForm]`
        correct: true
      - text: By reading `HttpContext.Request.Form` in `OnAfterRender`
    explanation: The model property is bound from the form data on POST. Initialise it with `Model ??= new()` so GET requests still have an instance.
  - id: antiforgery
    prompt: Which statements about antiforgery in Blazor Web Apps are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: "`EditForm` renders an antiforgery token automatically"
        correct: true
      - text: "`app.UseAntiforgery()` must be in the request pipeline"
        correct: true
      - text: "A plain `<form method=\"post\">` can include the token with the `<AntiforgeryToken />` component"
        correct: true
      - text: Antiforgery is only needed in WebAssembly apps
    explanation: Antiforgery protects form posts against cross-site request forgery in all server-rendered forms.
---
Static SSR pages have no live connection, yet forms still work — they post back to the server,
just like classic web apps, with Blazor handling binding and validation.

## Learning objectives

- Build forms that work without interactivity
- Bind posted data with `[SupplyParameterFromForm]`
- Use enhanced form posts for a smoother experience

## A static SSR form

```razor
@page "/contact"
@inject IContactService Contacts

<EditForm Model="Model" FormName="contact" OnValidSubmit="SubmitAsync" Enhance>
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
    <InputText @bind-Value="Model!.Name" placeholder="Name" />
    <ValidationMessage For="() => Model!.Name" />
    <InputTextArea @bind-Value="Model!.Message" />
    <button type="submit">Send</button>
</EditForm>

@if (sent)
{
    <p role="status">Thanks! We'll be in touch.</p>
}

@code {
    [SupplyParameterFromForm] private ContactModel? Model { get; set; }
    private bool sent;

    protected override void OnInitialized() => Model ??= new();

    private async Task SubmitAsync()
    {
        await Contacts.SendAsync(Model!);
        sent = true;
    }
}
```

On GET, `Model` is null and gets a fresh instance. On POST, Blazor binds the form fields into
`Model`, validates, and calls `OnValidSubmit`. No WebSocket and no WebAssembly are involved.

## Enhanced form handling

The `Enhance` parameter (or `data-enhance` on a plain `<form>`) makes `blazor.web.js` submit with
`fetch` and patch the page in place instead of a full reload — scroll position and unchanged DOM
are preserved.

## Plain HTML forms

```razor
<form method="post" @onsubmit="Subscribe" @formname="newsletter" data-enhance>
    <AntiforgeryToken />
    <input name="Email" type="email" />
    <button>Subscribe</button>
</form>

@code {
    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "newsletter")] private string? Email { get; set; }
    private Task Subscribe() => Newsletter.AddAsync(Email);
}
```

## When to choose static forms

Static forms are ideal for content sites, sign-in pages, contact forms and checkout steps: they
are fast, work before (or without) WebAssembly loads, and keep the server load low because no
circuit is held open.

## Learning objectives

- Write route templates with parameters and constraints
- Read query strings and navigate in code
- Handle not-found content correctly

## Route templates

```razor
@page "/products"
@page "/products/{Category}"
@page "/products/{Category}/{Id:int}"
@page "/files/{*Path}"
```

| Feature | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Parameter | `{Category}` → `[Parameter] public string? Category { get; set; }` |
| Constraint | `{Id:int}`, `{Date:datetime}`, `{Id:guid}`, `{Active:bool}` |
| Optional | `{Page:int?}` |
| Catch-all | `{*Path}` |

## Query strings

```razor
@page "/search"

@code {
    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "q")] public string? Query { get; set; }
    [SupplyParameterFromQuery] public int? Page { get; set; }
}
```

```csharp
var url = Navigation.GetUriWithQueryParameters(new Dictionary<string, object?>
{
    ["q"] = query,
    ["page"] = 2
});
Navigation.NavigateTo(url);
```

## Navigation

```razor
<NavLink href="orders" Match="NavLinkMatch.Prefix" ActiveClass="active">Orders</NavLink>
```

```csharp
Navigation.NavigateTo("/orders/42");
Navigation.NavigateTo("/login", forceLoad: true);    // full page load
Navigation.NavigateTo("/step-2", replace: true);     // replace history entry
```

## Not found (.NET 10)

```razor
<Router AppAssembly="typeof(Program).Assembly" NotFoundPage="typeof(Pages.NotFound)">
    <Found Context="routeData">
        <RouteView RouteData="routeData" DefaultLayout="typeof(Layout.MainLayout)" />
        <FocusOnNavigate RouteData="routeData" Selector="h1" />
    </Found>
</Router>
```

```csharp
protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
{
    product = await Catalog.FindAsync(Id);
    if (product is null) Navigation.NotFound();
}
```

During static SSR this sets a 404 status code; in interactive modes it renders the not-found page.
`FocusOnNavigate` moves focus to the page heading after navigation, which helps screen-reader users.

title: Enhanced navigation and streaming rendering
questions:

        correct: true
      - text: Converts the app into a WebAssembly app
      - text: Adds animations between pages

    options:

      - text: Use `<NavLink>` instead of `<a>`
      - id: data-enhance-nav

        correct: true
    explanation: Opt out where a page relies on scripts that expect a full load, or links to non-Blazor endpoints.
  - id: streaming
    prompt: What does `@attribute [StreamRendering]` do on a statically rendered page?
    options:
      - text: Streams video content
      - id: stream
        text: Sends the initial HTML immediately, then streams updated content over the same response when async work completes
        correct: true
      - text: Makes the page interactive
    explanation: Users see a loading placeholder at once instead of waiting for slow data before any HTML arrives.
  - id: permanent
    prompt: Which statements are true?
    type: multiple
    options:

        correct: true

        correct: true
      - text: Enhanced navigation keeps interactive components on the page alive when they still exist after the update
        correct: true

    explanation: Streaming is a static SSR feature that uses a single HTTP response.
---
## Learning objectives

- Understand enhanced navigation and how to opt out
- Use streaming rendering for slow data
- Preserve DOM regions across navigations

## Enhanced navigation

With `blazor.web.js` on the page, clicking an internal link triggers a `fetch` of the next page,
and Blazor patches the differences into the current DOM. The result feels like a single-page app,
while every page remains server-rendered HTML that search engines and no-JavaScript browsers can use.

```html
<a href="reports/export.csv" data-enhance-nav="false">Download CSV</a>
```

## Preserving regions

```html
<div data-permanent id="chat-widget">…</div>
```

Content marked `data-permanent` is left untouched by enhanced page updates — useful for
third-party widgets that keep their own state.

## Streaming rendering

```razor
@page "/weather"
@attribute [StreamRendering]

@if (forecasts is null)
{
    <p><em>Loading…</em></p>
}
else
{
    <table>
        @foreach (var f in forecasts)
        {
            <tr><td>@f.Date</td><td>@f.TemperatureC °C</td></tr>
        }
    </table>
}

@code {
    private WeatherForecast[]? forecasts;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync() =>
        forecasts = await Weather.GetForecastsAsync();
}
```

The server sends the page with "Loading…" immediately and keeps the response open. When
`OnInitializedAsync` completes, it streams the updated markup, and `blazor.web.js` swaps it in.

## Choosing the right tool

| Need | Use |
|------|-----|
| Fast pages, mostly content | Static SSR + enhanced navigation |
| Slow data on a static page | `[StreamRendering]` |
| Rich interaction (drag, live updates) | An interactive render mode for that component |

## Learning objectives

- Design components that load data in any render mode
- Use `IDbContextFactory` in Interactive Server
- Call APIs from WebAssembly with `HttpClient`

## The abstraction

```csharp
// Shared (e.g. Shop.Client or a Contracts library)
public interface IProductService
{
    Task<IReadOnlyList<ProductDto>> ListAsync(string? category, CancellationToken ct = default);
}
```

```csharp
// Server project
public sealed class ServerProductService(IDbContextFactory<ShopDbContext> factory) : IProductService
{
    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<ProductDto>> ListAsync(string? category, CancellationToken ct = default)
    {
        await using var db = await factory.CreateDbContextAsync(ct);
        return await db.Products
            .AsNoTracking()
            .Where(p => category == null || p.Category == category)
            .Select(p => new ProductDto(p.Id, p.Name, p.Price))
            .ToListAsync(ct);
    }
}
```

```csharp
// Client project
public sealed class HttpProductService(HttpClient http) : IProductService
{
    public async Task<IReadOnlyList<ProductDto>> ListAsync(string? category, CancellationToken ct = default) =>
        await http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<ProductDto>>($"api/products?category={Uri.EscapeDataString(category ?? "")}", ct) ?? [];
}
```

## Registration in each host

```csharp
// Server Program.cs
builder.Services.AddDbContextFactory<ShopDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(connectionString));
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ServerProductService>();
app.MapGet("/api/products", (string? category, IProductService products, CancellationToken ct) =>
    products.ListAsync(category, ct));

// Client Program.cs
builder.Services.AddScoped(sp => new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress) });
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, HttpProductService>();
```

## The component

```razor
@inject IProductService Products

@foreach (var p in products)
{
    <ProductCard Product="p" />
}

@code {
    [SupplyParameterFromQuery] public string? Category { get; set; }
    private IReadOnlyList<ProductDto> products = [];

    protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync() =>
        products = await Products.ListAsync(Category);
}
```

This is dependency inversion in practice: the component is reusable in every render mode — and in
a Hybrid app — because it never knows where its data comes from.

---
title: Persisting prerendered state
questions:
  - id: double-load
    prompt: Why might an interactive component with prerendering load its data twice?
    options:
      - id: twice
        text: The component initialises once during server prerendering and again when it becomes interactive, losing the first result
        correct: true
      - text: Because of a bug in `HttpClient`
      - text: Because `OnInitializedAsync` is never called
      - text: Because the browser refreshes automatically
    explanation: Without persisted state, the interactive instance starts from scratch and repeats the work, often causing a visible flicker.
  - id: persistent-state
    prompt: In .NET 10, what is the simplest way to carry prerendered data into the interactive component?
    options:
      - text: Store it in a static field
      - text: Write it to a cookie manually
      - id: attribute
        text: Mark a public property with `[PersistentState]`
        correct: true
    explanation: The framework serializes the property into the page during prerender and restores it when the component becomes interactive.
  - id: facts
    prompt: Which statements about persistent component state are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: The persisted data is embedded in the HTML sent to the browser, so it must not contain secrets
        correct: true
      - text: Earlier versions used the `PersistentComponentState` service with `RegisterOnPersisting` and `TryTakeFromJson`
        correct: true
      - text: Persisted values must be JSON-serializable
        correct: true
      - text: Persisted state survives a full browser refresh forever
    explanation: The state transfers once from prerender to interactive; it is not long-term storage.
---
## Learning objectives

- Explain why prerendering can cause double data loading
- Persist state with `[PersistentState]` (.NET 10)
- Use the lower-level `PersistentComponentState` service

## The problem

1. Server prerenders the page — `OnInitializedAsync` loads products, HTML is sent
2. The component starts interactively (circuit or WebAssembly) — a new instance runs
   `OnInitializedAsync` again, momentarily shows "Loading…", then reloads the products

## Declarative persistence (.NET 10)

```razor
@inject IProductService Products

@code {
    [PersistentState]
    public List<ProductDto>? Items { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        Items ??= [.. await Products.ListAsync(category: null)];
    }
}
```

During prerendering the property is serialized into the page. When the interactive instance
starts, the framework restores `Items` before `OnInitializedAsync` runs, so `??=` skips the second load.

## The underlying service

```razor
@implements IDisposable
@inject PersistentComponentState AppState

@code {
    private List<ProductDto>? items;
    private PersistingComponentStateSubscription subscription;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        subscription = AppState.RegisterOnPersisting(() =>
        {
            AppState.PersistAsJson("products", items);
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        });

        if (!AppState.TryTakeFromJson<List<ProductDto>>("products", out items))
        {
            items = [.. await Products.ListAsync(category: null)];
        }
    }

    public void Dispose() => subscription.Dispose();
}
```

## Guidelines

- Persist only what is needed to render, and never secrets — it is visible in page source
- Keep payloads small; they add to the HTML size
- Alternatively, disable prerendering for components where it adds little value

title: JavaScript interop and browser storage
